subject.title: [Bug]: GitHub Copilot anthropic-messages transport silently hangs ~365s in isolated cron sessions (2026.5.27)

question: Should OpenClaw treat aborted no-output embedded Copilot anthropic-messages runs as safe to fail over, or require a transport-level idle/progress fix before retrying another model?
rationale: The source still excludes aborted embedded results from result fallback because retries can duplicate side effects, while the reported cron path needs a recovery mechanism beyond the already-fixed status recording.

options.title: Prefer transport-level recovery
options.body: Require Copilot anthropic-messages to emit progress or fail early before changing aborted-result fallback semantics for all embedded runs.

options.title: Allow narrow aborted no-output fallback
options.body: Permit fallback only when the trace proves no tools, visible output, or delivery side effects occurred before the abort.

options.title: Close as partially fixed
options.body: Accept current cron error recording and configured-provider AbortError fallback as sufficient, leaving transport hangs to new narrower reports.

recommendation.title: Prefer transport-level recovery
recommendation.body: Require Copilot anthropic-messages to emit progress or fail early before changing aborted-result fallback semantics for all embedded runs.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest current history across Copilot Claude routing and adjacent provider/fallback surfaces.
